# graph-manager: start a run in a sandbox container, end to end (create, login copy, start, ready, live page, cleanup) (KAN-88)

## What to build

`POST /api/runs/:ws` with `{ tasksDir, spec, provider, concurrency?, sandbox: true }` starts the run in its own Docker container instead of spawning the engine on the server, and everything that shows a live run works for it: the Runs list (`live: true`), the run page through graph-manager's proxy, the view cache, and the "a run is live" check that blocks deleting a workspace. When the engine exits (Close on the run page, or the run is stopped), the container is removed and its record dropped.

Already in the codebase (earlier slices):

- Engine: `GRAPH_EXECUTION_WEB_HOST` / `GRAPH_EXECUTION_WEB_PORT` set the `--web-serve` page's bind address; `web.json` is `{ url: "http://127.0.0.1:<port>/", pid, host }` (`host` = `os.hostname()` of the writer); `GRAPH_EXECUTION_SANDBOX=1` + `GRAPH_EXECUTION_SANDBOX_IMAGE` make a new run save `sandbox: { image }` in `state.json`; the lock is `<pid>\n<token>\n<host>\n` and `graph-execution/api` exports `readLock(runDir)` → `{ pid, token?, host, foreign } | undefined`, `lockHost()`, `TAKE_LOCK_FROM_ENV`, `SANDBOX_ENV`, `SANDBOX_IMAGE_ENV`, `WEB_HOST_ENV`, `WEB_PORT_ENV`, `RUN_ID_ENV`.
- graph-manager: `src/server/docker.ts` (`DockerClient`: `createContainer(name, body)`, `putArchive(id, path, tar)`, `startContainer`, `inspectContainer` (404 → undefined), `stopContainer`, `removeContainer(id, { force })`, `waitContainer(id)` → exit code, `containerLogs(id, tail)`, `listContainers(label)`), `src/server/sandbox.ts` (`Sandboxes` with `docker`, `self` (own container or undefined), `init()`, `status()` → `{ available, reason?, defaultImage? }`, `defaultImage()`, `toolsMount()` → the read-only `/opt/gm-tools` mount, `SANDBOX_NETWORK = "gm-sandbox"`, `SANDBOX_PORT = 7600`), `src/server/sandbox-tools.ts`, `ctx.sandboxes` in `AppContext`, store keys `sandboxes` (record `{ runId, workspace, container, name, host, image, port, startedAt }`, key `${wsId}/${runId}`), `sandboxLimits` (`{ cpus, memoryMb, pids }`), `workspaceSettings` (`{ image?, sandbox? }` per workspace id), and the test fake `apps/graph-manager/scripts/fake-docker.mjs` (`startFakeDocker({ socketPath?, exec?, images?, self? })`; in `exec` mode a started container runs its `Cmd` as a local process with a loopback IP `127.0.0.<n>` that replaces `GRAPH_EXECUTION_WEB_HOST=0.0.0.0`, `/opt/gm-tools` bind targets rewritten to their host source, `HOME` rewritten to a per-container fake root where `/`-archives are extracted; without `exec` a start writes the ready file from `GRAPH_EXECUTION_READY_FILE` and stays running; `GET /__fake/state` dumps everything).

Spec: `docs/prd/sandboxes.md` — Requirements "startSandboxRun" (steps 1-3, the sandbox record), "graph-manager: runs, proxy, Start run, terminals" bullets 1, 3, 4; the provider login table; Decisions on mounts, env, user, network, liveness. KAN-89 (run options) edits the same start route in parallel: add `sandbox` as its own top-level body field (one line) and keep the sandbox branch in its own block.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/runs.ts` (whole file, 111 lines) — `startBody` (14-19), `INTERNAL_ENV` (22), `newRunId`, `insideWorkspace` (34-41), `lastLines` (48), the start route (74-110: args at 84, env 86-89, execa spawn 90-105, the 201 answer 109).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/runs.ts` (lines 19-37 `RunSummary`, 100-109 `isRunId`/`viewUrlOf`/`livePage`, 167-197 `summarize`, 204-220 listings, 419-449 `runDetail`, 452 `runDirOf`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/proxy.ts` (whole file, 83 lines) — `upstreamPort` (20-31), the hook (37-82): `livePage(dir)` at 54, Host rewrite at 60, `http.request({ host: "127.0.0.1", port, … })` at 64.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/viewcache.ts` (lines 217-297) — `ViewCache.poll()` and `save()`: `livePage(runDir)` at 269, fetches `${base}state` with `this.fetchFn` at 272.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/workspaces.ts` (lines 105-127 `liveRunPid`, used at 293 by `DELETE /api/workspaces/:id`).
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.ts`, `docker.ts`, `store.ts`, `app.ts` — the service, client, schema and context you extend.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/runs.test.ts` (lines 1-110) — the start-run test setup: a real built engine (`defaultGraphExecutionBin()`, `it.skipIf(!built)`), a workspace with the committed `diamond` fixture and `spec.md`, a listening app with a cookie, `poll(what, fn)`.
- `apps/graph-manager/src/server/proxy.test.ts` (lines 1-80) — a fake upstream that checks `Host: 127.0.0.1:<port>`.
- `apps/graph-manager/Dockerfile` (lines 36-40) — graph-manager runs as UID 1000 with `HOME=/data/home`; `/data` holds `graph-manager.json` (forge tokens). None of it may reach a sandbox.

## Patterns to follow

The current start (routes/runs.ts:83-109), which the non-sandbox branch keeps as is:

```ts
const runId = newRunId();
const args = [body.tasksDir, "--spec", body.spec, "--provider", body.provider, "--web"];
if (body.concurrency !== undefined) args.push("--concurrency", String(body.concurrency));
const env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = { ...process.env, GRAPH_EXECUTION_HANDOFF: "detached", SSH_CONNECTION: "1", [RUN_ID_ENV]: runId };
...
return reply.code(201).send({ runId: id, viewUrl: viewUrlOf(ws.id, id) });
```

Error answers of the start route: `reply.code(400).send({ error, exitCode?, output? })` — the Start run drawer shows `output` under the title.

Store updates: `await ctx.store.update((d) => { d.sandboxes[key] = rec; })` (validated, written atomically, mode 600).

## Step-by-step tasks

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/tar.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT** `export interface TarEntry { path: string; dir?: boolean; content?: Buffer; mode?: number }` and `export function tarArchive(entries: TarEntry[], owner: { uid: number; gid: number }): Buffer` — a POSIX ustar writer: 512-byte header per entry (name ≤ 100 bytes, else split into `prefix` (≤155) + `name`; mode / uid / gid / size / mtime as zero-padded octal with a trailing NUL; typeflag `"0"` file or `"5"` dir; magic `"ustar\0"`, version `"00"`; checksum computed with the checksum field as 8 spaces, written as 6 octal digits + NUL + space), the content padded to 512, and two zero blocks at the end. Directory paths end with `/`.
- **TEST** `tar.test.ts`: write an archive to a temp file and list it with `tar -tvf` (execa): names, sizes and a `dir/` entry are right; extract with `tar -xf` and compare contents; a 130-char path round-trips.

### CREATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox-run.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT** the pure parts, each exported for tests:
  - `export const LOGIN_FILES: Record<string, string[]>` — `claude: [".claude/.credentials.json", ".claude.json"]`, `codex: [".codex/auth.json", ".codex/config.toml"]`, `opencode: [".local/share/opencode/auth.json", ".config/opencode/"]` (a trailing `/` = a folder, copied recursively), `qwen: [".qwen/oauth_creds.json", ".qwen/settings.json"]`, `fake: []`.
  - `export const LOGIN_KEYS: Record<string, string[]>` — `claude: ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN"]`, `codex: ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]`, `opencode: ["OPENAI_API_KEY", "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"]`, `qwen: ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]`, `fake: []`.
  - `export async function loginEntries(providers: string[], home: string, env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv): Promise<TarEntry[]>` — for each provider (the run's provider; reviewers are a later feature and will add theirs), the files of `LOGIN_FILES` that exist under `home`, as entries `home/sandbox/<rel>` (plus the parent directory entries `home/`, `home/sandbox/`, `home/sandbox/.claude/` …, mode `0o700`; files `0o600`). A provider other than `fake` with none of its files and none of its `LOGIN_KEYS` set throws `SandboxError(400, \`no ${p} login to copy into the sandbox: log in once in a terminal, or set ${LOGIN_KEYS[p][0]}\`)`. Always include `home/` and `home/sandbox/` so HOME exists in any image.
  - `export function sandboxEnv(base: NodeJS.ProcessEnv, p: { runId: string; runDir: string; image: string; takeLockFrom?: string; gitIdentity?: Record<string, string> }): string[]` — `KEY=value` strings:
    - from `base`, only: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK`, `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX`, `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`, `GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`, `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME`, `GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL`, `TZ`, `LANG`, and every `GRAPH_EXECUTION_*` except the internal ones (`GRAPH_EXECUTION_RUNS_ROOT`, `_READY_FILE`, `_TASK_NAME`, `_RUN_ID`, `_HANDOFF`, `_TAKE_LOCK_FROM`, `_SANDBOX`, `_SANDBOX_IMAGE`, `_WEB_HOST`, `_WEB_PORT`). Never any `GM_*` (they hold the password), never `HOME`, `PATH`, `HOSTNAME`.
    - the four `GIT_*` identity vars from `gitIdentity` when `base` lacks them;
    - then: `GRAPH_EXECUTION_SANDBOX=1`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_SANDBOX_IMAGE=<image>`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_RUN_ID=<runId>`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_WEB_HOST=0.0.0.0`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_WEB_PORT=7600`, `GRAPH_EXECUTION_READY_FILE=<runDir>/.ready.json`, `HOME=/home/sandbox`, `PATH=/opt/gm-tools/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin`, and `GRAPH_EXECUTION_TAKE_LOCK_FROM=<host>` when `takeLockFrom` is set. (Docker does not expand `$PATH` in `Env`; this is the Debian default path.)
  - `export async function gitIdentity(cwd: string): Promise<Record<string, string>>` — `git config --get user.name` / `user.email` in the workspace (execa, `reject: false`); returns `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/EMAIL` + `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME/EMAIL` for the values found. (Inside the sandbox `HOME` is empty, so the server's global git identity must come in as env.)
  - `export function workspaceMount(ws: Workspace, workspacesDir: string, self: ContainerInfo | undefined, override?: string)` → a Docker `Mounts` entry:
    - `override` (`config.sandboxWorkspacesSource`): absolute → `{ Type: "bind", Source: path.posix.join(override, ws.rel), Target: ws.path }`; else a volume name → `{ Type: "volume", Source: override, Target: ws.path, VolumeOptions: { Subpath: ws.rel } }`;
    - `self` set: its mount with `Destination === path.resolve(workspacesDir)`: `volume` → `{ Type: "volume", Source: m.Name, Target: ws.path, VolumeOptions: { Subpath: ws.rel } }`; `bind` → `{ Type: "bind", Source: path.posix.join(m.Source, ws.rel), Target: ws.path }`; none → throw `SandboxError(400, "graph-manager's workspaces folder is not a Docker mount: set GM_SANDBOX_WORKSPACES_SOURCE")`;
    - no `self`: `{ Type: "bind", Source: ws.path, Target: ws.path }`.
    The workspace is always mounted read-write at the SAME absolute path (git worktrees and state.json store absolute paths); other workspaces are never visible.
  - `export class SandboxError extends Error { constructor(readonly status: number, message: string, readonly output?: string) }`.
  - `export function containerBody(p)` → the create body: `{ Image, Hostname, User: "<uid>:<gid>", Env, Cmd: ["node", "/opt/gm-tools/graph-execution/dist/cli.js", ...args, "--web-serve"], WorkingDir: cwd, Labels: { "gm.run": runId, "gm.workspace": ws.id }, HostConfig: { Init: true, NanoCpus: Math.round(cpus * 1e9), Memory: memoryMb * 1024 * 1024, PidsLimit: pids, SecurityOpt: ["no-new-privileges"], AutoRemove: false, NetworkMode: "gm-sandbox", Mounts: [workspace, tools] } }`.
- **GOTCHA**: no tmpfs at `/home/sandbox`: a tmpfs is mounted when the container starts and would hide the login files copied in before. The container's own writable layer holds the home and is removed with the container.
- **GOTCHA**: `AutoRemove: false` on purpose: graph-manager waits for the container (`waitContainer`), reads its logs when it failed to start, then removes it itself. With AutoRemove the logs would be gone.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/sandbox.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT** on `Sandboxes`:
  - `async start(p: { ws: Workspace; cwd: string; args: string[]; runId: string; providers: string[]; takeLockFrom?: string; image?: string; readyTimeoutMs?: number }): Promise<SandboxRecord>`:
    1. `const st = await this.status(); if (!st.available) throw new SandboxError(400, st.reason ?? "sandboxes are not available")`.
    2. image = `p.image || store.workspaceSettings[ws.id]?.image || this.defaultImage()`; none → `SandboxError(400, "no sandbox image: set one for the workspace, or GM_SANDBOX_IMAGE")`.
    3. `runDir = runDirOf(ws, runId)`; `rm(<runDir>/.ready.json, { force: true })`.
    4. owner = `stat(ws.path)` uid/gid; `host = "sbx-" + randomBytes(4).toString("hex")`; name `gm-run-<runId>` (when a container of that name exists and is not running, remove it first; when it is running → `SandboxError(409, "the run's sandbox is still running")`).
    5. `createContainer(name, containerBody(...))` with limits from `store.get().sandboxLimits`, env `sandboxEnv(process.env, { runId, runDir, image, takeLockFrom, gitIdentity: await gitIdentity(ws.path) })`, mounts `[workspaceMount(...), this.toolsMount()!]`.
    6. `putArchive(id, "/", tarArchive(await loginEntries(p.providers, os.homedir(), process.env), owner))` — on any error from here on, remove the container before rethrowing.
    7. `startContainer(id)`, then save the record `{ runId, workspace: ws.id, container: id, name, host, image, port: SANDBOX_PORT, startedAt }` under `${ws.id}/${runId}` and start the watcher (below).
    8. Wait up to `readyTimeoutMs ?? 60_000` for `<runDir>/.ready.json` (poll every 250 ms): present → return the record. The container is no longer running (inspect) → `logs = await containerLogs(id, 20)`, remove container + record, throw `SandboxError(400, \`the sandbox exited with code ${code}\`, logs)`. Timeout → logs, `stopContainer` + remove + drop record, throw `SandboxError(400, "the sandbox did not start within 60 s", logs)`.
  - Watcher: `private watch(rec)` → `docker.waitContainer(rec.container).then(async () => { await docker.removeContainer(rec.container).catch(() => {}); await dropRecord(key) })`, once per container id (keep a `Set` of watched ids; errors are swallowed). `dropRecord` deletes the key only while it still points at that container id.
  - In `init()`, after the network/tools steps: reconcile the stored records: for each, `inspectContainer`: missing → drop the record; not running → remove the container, drop the record; running → `watch(rec)`.
  - `async pageOf(runDir: string): Promise<SandboxPage | null | undefined>` — `undefined` when no record maps to this run dir (not a sandboxed run as far as graph-manager knows); `null` when the record's container is not running; else `{ url: "http://127.0.0.1:7600/", pid: 0, upstream: { host: <IPAddress on gm-sandbox, or the first network's IPAddress>, port: rec.port } }`. Map run dirs with `resolveWorkspace(config.workspacesDir, rec.workspace)` + `path.join(ws.path, RUNS_DIR, rec.runId)`. Cache inspect results for 1 s per container.
  - `recordOf(wsId, runId)` returns the record or undefined.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/runs.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `export interface LivePage { url: string; pid: number; /** Where the proxy connects; absent = 127.0.0.1:<port of url>. */ upstream?: { host: string; port: number } }`.
  - `export interface SandboxLookup { pageOf(runDir: string): Promise<LivePage | null | undefined> }`, a module-level `let sandboxLookup: SandboxLookup | undefined` and `export function setSandboxLookup(l: SandboxLookup | undefined): void`.
  - `livePage(runDir)`: `const s = await sandboxLookup?.pageOf(runDir); if (s !== undefined) return s ?? undefined;` then as today, plus: a `web.json` whose `host` is set and differs from `os.hostname()` is not live (it was written in a container whose record is gone; its pid means nothing here).
  - `RunSummary` gets `/** Set for a run graph-manager started in a sandbox while its container exists. */ sandbox?: { running: boolean }` — in `summarize`, `sandboxLookup?.pageOf(entry.dir)`: `undefined` → no field; `null` → `{ running: false }`; a page → `{ running: true }` (reuse the same call that decides `live`).
- **GOTCHA**: `buildApp` calls `setSandboxLookup(sandboxes)` and an `onClose` hook calls `setSandboxLookup(undefined)`; vitest runs each test file in its own module graph, so the global does not leak between files.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/proxy.ts` and `viewcache.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - proxy: `const target = web?.upstream ?? (port !== undefined ? { host: "127.0.0.1", port } : undefined)`; 404 as today when undefined; `headers.host = \`127.0.0.1:${target.port}\`` (unchanged rule: the engine's Host check accepts only 127.0.0.1:<port>); `http.request({ host: target.host, port: target.port, … })`.
  - Export `export function upstreamGetJson(target: { host: string; port: number }, pathname: string, timeoutMs: number): Promise<unknown>` (node:http, `Host: 127.0.0.1:<port>`, rejects on non-200 / timeout).
  - viewcache `save()`: when `page.upstream` is set, read the state with `upstreamGetJson(page.upstream, "/state", 2000)` instead of `this.fetchFn` (fetch cannot set `Host`).
- **GOTCHA**: keep `upstreamPort` exported and unchanged (tests use it).

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/workspaces.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT** in `liveRunPid` (105-127): read each run's lock with `readLock` from `graph-execution/api`; for a `foreign` lock, never `process.kill` its pid; instead the run counts as live when `ctx.sandboxes?.pageOf(runDir)` returns a page. Also count any `sandboxes` record of this workspace whose container is running (use `pageOf`). Pass what it needs (`ctx`) as a parameter.

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/routes/runs.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `startBody` gets one line: `sandbox: z.boolean().optional(),` (after `concurrency`).
  - After the path checks and `const runId = newRunId();`, a separate block:
    ```ts
    if (body.sandbox === true) {
      if (!ctx.sandboxes) return reply.code(400).send({ error: "sandboxes are not set up" });
      const args = [body.tasksDir, "--spec", body.spec, "--provider", body.provider];
      if (body.concurrency !== undefined) args.push("--concurrency", String(body.concurrency));
      try {
        await ctx.sandboxes.start({ ws, cwd: ws.path, args, runId, providers: [body.provider] });
      } catch (err) {
        if (err instanceof SandboxError) return reply.code(err.status).send({ error: err.message, ...(err.output ? { output: lastLines(err.output, 20) } : {}) });
        throw err;
      }
      await rememberSandbox(ctx, ws.id, true);
      return reply.code(201).send({ runId, viewUrl: viewUrlOf(ws.id, runId) });
    }
    ```
  - After a successful plain start, `await rememberSandbox(ctx, ws.id, false)`. `rememberSandbox` = `ctx.store.update((d) => { d.workspaceSettings[id] = { ...d.workspaceSettings[id], sandbox: on }; })`.
- **GOTCHA**: never pass `--web` into the container (`--web-serve` is appended by `containerBody`).

### UPDATE `apps/graph-manager/src/server/app.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: `setSandboxLookup(sandboxes)` after creating it; `app.addHook("onClose", async () => setSandboxLookup(undefined))`.

### CREATE tests

- `sandbox-run.test.ts` (pure): `sandboxEnv` drops `GM_PASSWORD`, `GM_PORT`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`-like unrelated vars, keeps `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `GRAPH_EXECUTION_REVIEWERS_FILE`, drops `GRAPH_EXECUTION_RUNS_ROOT`, sets the sandbox vars and `TAKE_LOCK_FROM` only when given; `workspaceMount` for the three cases (override path, override volume, self volume with `Subpath: "github/octo/hello"`, self bind, no self, self without a mount → `SandboxError`); `loginEntries(["claude"], home)` with `home/.claude/.credentials.json` → entries `home/sandbox/.claude/.credentials.json` (mode 0o600) and its dirs; with no files and no key → error text `no claude login to copy into the sandbox: log in once in a terminal, or set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set and no files → only the home dirs; `fake` → only the home dirs; `containerBody` puts `Memory: 4096 * 1024 * 1024`, `NanoCpus: 2e9`, `PidsLimit: 2048`, `SecurityOpt: ["no-new-privileges"]`, `Init: true`, `NetworkMode: "gm-sandbox"`, `Cmd` ending in `--web-serve`.
- `routes/runs.sandbox.test.ts` (route level, fake Docker WITHOUT exec): `appWithLogin({ dockerSocket })` with a workspace containing committed `diamond` + `spec.md`; POST `{ tasksDir: "diamond", spec: "spec.md", provider: "fake", sandbox: true }` → 201 `{ runId, viewUrl }`; the fake has one container named `gm-run-<runId>` with labels `gm.run`/`gm.workspace`, `Image` = the workspace image (set `store.update(d => d.workspaceSettings[WS] = { image: "img:ws" })`) or `config.sandboxImage`, `User` = `<uid>:<gid>` of the workspace folder, `WorkingDir` = the workspace path, `HostConfig.Memory` = the stored `sandboxLimits.memoryMb` × 1048576 (store 8192 first → 8589934592), mounts = workspace bind at the same path + tools read-only; `Env` has no entry starting with `GM_`; the store has the record and `workspaceSettings[WS].sandbox === true`. With an unreachable socket → 400 with `error` starting `Docker is not reachable`. No image anywhere → 400 `no sandbox image`. A fake container that "exits" before ready (use a fake without exec and delete the ready-file behaviour by giving the container an env without `GRAPH_EXECUTION_READY_FILE`? simpler: pass `readyTimeoutMs` via a test hook such as `ctx.sandboxes.readyTimeoutMs = 500`) → 400 `the sandbox did not start within 60 s` and the container is removed.
- `sandbox.e2e.test.ts` — `describe.skipIf(process.platform !== "linux" || !built)` with the fake Docker in **exec** mode and the real built engine (`npm run build -w graph-execution` first): start a sandboxed fake run through the HTTP API (listening app, as `routes/runs.test.ts`) → 201; `GET /api/runs` lists it with `live: true` and `sandbox: { running: true }` within 30 s; `GET /runs/<ws>/<runId>/view/state` through the proxy answers 200 JSON with the run id; poll `state.json` until `status` is `applied`; `POST /runs/<ws>/<runId>/view/close` (with `origin` = the app's base URL) → the fake's container is gone (removed) within 10 s and the store has no record; `GET /api/runs` shows `live: false` and no `sandbox` field; the workspace has the applied files `1.txt`…`4.txt` uncommitted; `DELETE /api/workspaces/<ws>` answers 409 while the run is live (check before Close).
- Extend `proxy.test.ts`: with a stub `setSandboxLookup({ pageOf: async () => ({ url: "http://127.0.0.1:7600/", pid: 0, upstream: { host: "127.0.0.1", port: <fake upstream port> } }) })` the proxy reaches the fake upstream with `Host: 127.0.0.1:<that port>`; with `pageOf → null` the view answers 404 "the run's page is not running". Reset with `setSandboxLookup(undefined)` in `afterEach`.
- Extend `runs.test.ts` (server/runs.test.ts): a `web.json` with `host: "other-host"` and `pid: process.pid` is not live.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `POST /api/runs/:ws` with `sandbox: true` → 201 `{ runId, viewUrl }`; the container is `gm-run-<runId>` with the workspace (rw, same path) and the tools (ro) mounted, the limits from `sandboxLimits`, `no-new-privileges`, `Init`, network `gm-sandbox`, the workspace owner's uid:gid, and no `GM_*` env.
- [ ] The provider's login files are copied into `/home/sandbox` (only those that exist); a provider with no login and no key fails with the spec's message.
- [ ] The run is `live` while its container runs, its page works through `/runs/<ws>/<id>/view/`, and the view cache records it.
- [ ] When the engine exits, the container is removed and the record dropped; nothing is left behind.
- [ ] A start that fails before the page is ready answers 400 with the last 20 log lines in `output` and leaves no container.
- [ ] `workspaceSettings[<ws>].sandbox` is saved on every successful start.
- [ ] Delete of a workspace is refused while its sandbox runs; a foreign lock pid is never signalled.
- [ ] Tests pass: `npm run build -w graph-execution && npm test -w graph-manager -- sandbox runs proxy tar workspaces`

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run build -w graph-execution
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm test -w graph-manager -- sandbox runs proxy tar workspaces viewcache
npm test
```
